Class ClientController

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.am14.clientModelController.ClientController
public class ClientController extends Object
The primary controller on the client side, orchestrating network requests and local model sync.

This class acts as the mediator between the user view (UI/CLI), the local ClientModel, and the remote infrastructure represented by the VirtualServer proxy. It enforces defensive, "fail-fast" business rules (checking turn validity, available card indexes, constraints) before uploading actions to the network. Additionally, it implements low-level background heartbeat routines (Ping/Pong tracking) to handle connection losses or timeouts cleanly.

  • Method Details

    • pickCard

      public void pickCard(int cardId)
      Attempts to pick a card from the board grid layout on behalf of the home player.

      Before sending the action across the network proxy, the routine enforces a sequence of local defensive guards:

      • Ensures an active server session link exists.
      • Checks whether the game is currently inside a valid picking phase.
      • Validates that the selected unique ID lies within legal card indices (cardId <= 116).
      • Enforces specific game rules (e.g., preventing explicit collection of structural Event cards between indices 84 and 95).
      • Verifies if it is currently this player's turn to act.
      • Calculates row addresses to confirm structural eligibility and available resources.
      Any failed rule alerts the view subsystem via ExceptionViewEvent without hitting the network thread.
      Parameters:
      cardId - the unique identification index of the card being drafted

    • checkPing

      public void checkPing()
      Launches a dedicated background watchdog thread that loops at regular intervals to monitor connection liveness.

      If the delta duration between the current clock value and the lastPingReceived registry exceeds the configured timeout parameter, it triggers an automated crash disconnect cycle, interrupts downstream sub-threads, and gracefully terminates itself to protect application stability.
